newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Apr 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials - Apr 4.

text.p: There are 88 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the international community was watching how Hong Kong Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa was going to amend two human rights ordinances, which would put his political capability to test. It said that Tung should be more open-minded on this issue and release more details over his proposal to ban political parties from receiving foreign donations in the future.

-- The Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO said what had happened in Hong Kong in the seven years since the establishment of the Basic Law had proved that it could guarantee the carrying out of the "one country, two systems" principle. The paper said that Hong Kong people would enjoy more freedom after the handover than they had under the British colonial government.

-- The English-language HONGKONG STANDARD said Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa was faced with the problem of having responsibility but no power. That was why he needed to tread carefully and not spell out policies unless they had been fully thought through. He should be selective and choose only those functions and meetings that were really important to mark his presence, the paper said.
